findings.why: 'Say goodbye to dark spots' implies the spots are gone for good, an absolute result in the most-read field. It is also an agitation framing (TON-01).
findings.fix: Helps fade the look of dark spots

findings.why: Glutathione is widely marketed in India as a skin-whitening active. Pairing it with 'even out skin tone' and 'restore your natural glow' risks being read as a lightening claim. It is acceptable if the copy stays clearly on dark spots and an even-looking tone.
findings.fix: Keep the copy scoped to the look of dark spots, e.g. 'for a more even-looking tone', and have the reviewer confirm the active isn't being positioned for lightening.

findings.why: Both actives are named without concentrations, which is the brand's signature detail.
findings.fix: State the concentrations as on the pack, e.g. '[x]% Kojic Acid and [y]% Glutathione'.

rule_hit_review.why: 'Say goodbye to' is a problem-agitation framing; it also implies an absolute result, raised separately under CLM-03.
'remove dark spots' is an elimination verb applied to a skin concern.
'restore your natural glow' uses natural framing, which runs against the brand's position.

tone_read: The 'Say goodbye to…' headline with an exclamation mark is a category-style hook rather than Minimalist's calm, declarative voice. The body is short and names the actives, which helps.
language_read: The actives are named but without concentrations, and efficacy is unhedged ('remove dark spots, even out skin tone'). 'Natural glow' framing is off-brand.
